title: Advance Durable Goods Orders (Nov 2026 data)
source: CENSUS: two primaries fetched direct 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research — census.gov/manufacturing/m3/release_schedule.html, whose terminal grid row decodes to 'November 2026 | 12/23/2026 | TBD' (advance report, then the full report, which has no date yet), and census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html, which carries 'Advance Report on Durable Goods--Manufacturers' Shipments, Inventories, and Orders | December 23, 2026 | 8:30 AM | November 2026', id A202612230830. Filed estimate on 2026-09-04 solely because this lane never self-confirms an event in the PR that discovers it; its own initial research is the named condition for the flip. TWO BOUNDARIES ON THE WORD: `confirmed` describes the published schedule as of 2026-09-05, not immunity from a re-dating, and emphatically NOT immunity from the funding branch below — a lapse-driven slip is a schedule change Census makes unilaterally and this label does not price it
notes: THE EDITION THE FUNDING RISK MIGRATED TO, AND ITS BRANCH IS STILL OPEN. H.R. 6500 (signed 2026-09-02) funds the government only through 2026-12-11 and this release lands 12 days past that cliff; as of 2026-09-05 none of the 12 FY2027 appropriations bills has cleared Congress (3 passed the House, 0 reported from Senate Appropriations). The predecessor durable-goods-2026-10-27 closed its own branch by signature; this one cannot, because that signature CREATED the cliff it sits behind. WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDED (docs/research/events/durable-goods-2026-12-23.md, 2026-09-05), all three findings measured rather than carried: (1) the 2025 delay tail is longer and worse-targeted than this entry was filed with — read off the M3 grid, publication lag from reference-month end went 25d steady-state -> 57d (Sep-2025) -> 53d (Oct) -> 57d (NOV, +34d vs the year-ago slot, this print's exact analogue and the worst-hit, landing 2026-01-26) -> 49 -> 41 -> 38 -> 29 -> 28 -> 25d, i.e. EIGHT reference months to normalize, with every month carrying a date: delayed, never deleted. (2) That is a property of THIS SERIES, not of Census — the same calendar page reads 'Suspended' for Advance Economic Indicators (Jan + Feb 2026) and Preliminary Steel Imports (Dec 2025 + Jan 2026), while BEA CANCELLED the 2025 analogue of the PCE print sharing this exact 08:30 slot. Three documented failure modes on one morning. (3) The session is the most reliably compressed regular session of the year and it is measured ON the configuration, not argued into it: across 33 years the last full session before Christmas runs ~35% narrower than an ordinary session (SPY range p19, QQQ p17; null control p46), and on the TEN Nov-data release dates recovered verbatim from Census press releases (8 of 10 land exactly on that session) it is p23 / 0.688x with a mean close-to-close of +0.03% SPY and -0.13% QQQ. NOT TRADEABLE, and the 08:30 slot is triple-booked with a high-tier confirmed PCE plus the Q3 GDP third estimate. Note the coincidence of dates is not an error: 2025-12-23 was the DELAYED slot for October-2025 data, and 2026-12-23 is the ORDINARY slot for November-2026 data. Discovered during the durable-goods-2026-10-27 initial research (2026-09-04); researched 2026-09-05.
